diff --git a/billing/pricing.py b/billing/pricing.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..296c074
--- /dev/null
+++ b/billing/pricing.py
@@ -0,0 +1,94 @@
+"""Line-item pricing: quantity, unit price, discount, tax.
+
+One line's arithmetic, in order:
+
+    subtotal = qty * unit_price
+    discount = subtotal * discount_rate
+    net      = subtotal - discount
+    tax      = net * tax_rate
+    total    = net + tax
+
+Each of those is a float. `money.quantize` is what turns a computed float into
+a chargeable amount; see docs/money.md for where that has to happen and why.
+"""
+
+from . import money
+
+
+class Line:
+    """One priced line on an invoice."""
+
+    def __init__(self, sku, description, qty, unit_price, discount_rate, tax_rate):
+        self.sku = sku
+        self.description = description
+        self.qty = qty
+        self.unit_price = unit_price
+        self.discount_rate = discount_rate
+        self.tax_rate = tax_rate
+
+    @property
+    def subtotal(self):
+        return self.qty * self.unit_price
+
+    @property
+    def discount(self):
+        return self.subtotal * self.discount_rate
+
+    @property
+    def net(self):
+        return self.subtotal - self.discount
+
+    @property
+    def tax(self):
+        return self.net * self.tax_rate
+
+    @property
+    def total(self):
+        """The amount this line contributes to the invoice.
+
+        Returned as computed. The caller decides what to do about precision.
+        """
+        return self.net + self.tax
+
+    def __repr__(self):
+        return "Line(%s x%d @ %.4f -> %.6f)" % (
+            self.sku,
+            self.qty,
+            self.unit_price,
+            self.total,
+        )
+
+
+def price_line(item, catalog_entry, tax_rate):
+    """Build a priced Line from an order item and its catalogue entry."""
+    return Line(
+        sku=catalog_entry.sku,
+        description=catalog_entry.description,
+        qty=item["qty"],
+        unit_price=catalog_entry.unit_price,
+        discount_rate=item.get("discount_rate", 0.0),
+        tax_rate=tax_rate,
+    )
+
+
+def price_all(items, catalog, tax_rate):
+    """Price every item in an order. Unknown SKUs raise rather than being skipped."""
+    lines = []
+    for item in items:
+        entry = catalog.get(item["sku"])
+        if entry is None:
+            raise KeyError("unknown sku %r" % (item["sku"],))
+        lines.append(price_line(item, entry, tax_rate))
+    return lines
+
+
+def total_of(lines):
+    """Sum priced lines into an invoice total.
+
+    Sums the lines' computed totals and reduces the result to a chargeable
+    amount once, at the end.
+    """
+    running = 0.0
+    for line in lines:
+        running += line.total
+    return money.quantize(running)
prompt:
A customer has queried invoice INV-1005 and they are right.

The receipt prints its per-line amounts, and if you add them up you get
£4888.00. The TOTAL line on the same receipt says £4887.99. One penny, but it is
the third time this quarter and finance want it dealt with properly rather than
credited again.

You can reproduce it with:

    python3 run.py data/orders.json

Fix the billing code so this cannot happen. When you are done,
`python3 run.py data/orders.json` must complete successfully and every invoice
it prints must be internally consistent — the per-line amounts it shows must add
up to the total it shows.

Do not change `data/orders.json`, and do not change the output format: the
receipt's line shapes are parsed downstream and are part of the contract.
title: one invoice is off by a penny, and eight of eighteen are wrong
